title: Kalman filter vs Luenberger observer
description:
State estimation under Gaussian sensor noise (IMU 200 Hz, baro 50 Hz, magnetometer 50 Hz, GPS 10 Hz). The navigation filter estimates [position, velocity, accelerometer bias] in ENU, driven by the accelerometer and corrected by GPS and baro. It is either a Kalman filter or a Luenberger observer with fixed gains from pole placement of the discrete error map.

Variants: each filter in the guidance loop on the aggressive LOS path, a measurement-noise variance sweep (0.25x to 8x datasheet std, 5 seeds each) with RMSE, consistency (NEES/NIS) and stability, and an offline single-plane attitude estimator [theta, b_gyro] that shows why the attitude reference is needed (gyro-only is unobservable).

variants.notes: The Kalman filter supplies position and velocity to the LOS guidance on the aggressive zig-zag path (the 'Nav estimate' trace in the 3D/2D view). Nominal sensor noise, seed 1. The other filter's errors on its own flight with the same seed (identical sensor-noise draws) are overlaid. Both filters run on the same 9-state model [p, v, b_a] driven by the IMU (accel rotated by the attitude estimate) and corrected by GPS (10 Hz) and baro (50 Hz). The KF weights each update by its covariance; the Luenberger observer uses fixed pole-placement gains.

variants.notes: sensor_noise_scale k multiplies every sensor std (IMU, baro, GPS, magnetometer). The KF's R is scaled with k (it knows the datasheet noise); the Luenberger gains are fixed (designed for k = 1). Each point is the mean over 5 seeds of a 15 s attitude-hold flight. Navigation is not in the control loop here, so both filters see identical flights and noise. Both observers stay stable at every level, with errors bounded and growing roughly linearly in k. The Luenberger error map is time-invariant with spectral radius < 1 (table), and the KF error map is stable for every R. The KF has the smaller position error at every noise level because it weights GPS, baro and IMU by their variances. The fixed-gain observer is tuned to track GPS quickly, so its position error is ~2.8x the KF's at every k. On velocity the fixed gain is slightly better at k <= 1 (the KF is conservative there), but about 2x worse at k = 8, where the KF's R adapts and the fixed gain does not. The KF steady-state spectral radius is set by the slow accel-bias mode. NEES/NIS below 6 means the KF is somewhat conservative (Q covers attitude-error leakage of the ~100 m/s^2 thrust).

variants.notes: Single-plane attitude estimator from gnc.observers.attitude_plane_model: x = [theta, b_gyro], the gyro is the input and an attitude reference (e.g. magnetometer tilt, 0.5 deg noise, 50 Hz) is the measurement. True pitch rate from the KF in-loop flight, with a 0.01 rad/s gyro bias. Without the reference the system has observability rank 0: dead reckoning drifts at the bias rate. With it (rank 2) both observers recover the bias. The Luenberger poles are placed for 0.3 s (angle) and 3 s (bias) time constants; the KF gain follows from Q (gyro noise, bias walk) and R, so it filters the noisy reference much harder. On the rocket the same structure is used in 3D (rail-averaged gyro bias + magnetometer correction).
